title: How many pairs to reorder?
summary: Work out the order quantity that tops each style up to its target cover, without ever ordering a negative number.

blocks.text: The buyer wants a reorder list by noon. For each style the rule is simple: stock plus pairs already on order should cover the next 6 weeks of sales. If it already does, order nothing.
You will write one formula that works out the shortfall and never returns a negative order.

items: Objective: calculate a reorder quantity and floor it at zero with MAX.
You pass the mission at 75% or more in the Assessment.

blocks.formula: =target weeks x weekly sales - on hand - on order
blocks.text: The stock you need over the target period, minus what you already hold, minus what is already on its way. The answer is the shortfall.
G2 holds the target cover in weeks. The dollar signs lock G2, so the same target is used on every row when you copy the formula down.
Problem: a style that is already overstocked gives a negative number, and you cannot order minus 50 pairs. You need the answer floored at zero.
MAX returns the larger of its values. MAX(0, shortfall) gives the shortfall when it is positive and 0 when it is negative.
IF can do the same job, but you have to write the sum twice. MAX is shorter and easier to check.
Tip: always subtract pairs on order. If you ignore them you order the same stock twice.
Four questions on reorder quantities. Type numbers without commas, for example 60.

items: Reorder = target weeks x weekly sales - on hand - on order.
Keep the target weeks in one cell and lock it with $ signs.
MAX(0, x) floors a result at zero, so you never order a negative quantity.
Always count pairs already on order.

blocks.text: Next: size-curve share, to see which sizes carry the sales.

items.prompt: A style sells 20 pairs a week. The target is 8 weeks of cover, with 70 pairs on hand and 30 on order. How many pairs should you reorder?
A style sells 15 pairs a week. The target is 6 weeks, with 100 pairs on hand and none on order. What does =MAX(0,6*15-100-0) return?
Why wrap the shortfall in MAX(0, ...)?

options.label: A style that is already overstocked gives a negative number, and MAX turns that into 0 pairs
It rounds the order up to a whole case
It doubles the quantity for safety
It changes the number into text

items.prompt: Why subtract the pairs already on order as well as the pairs on hand?

options.label: Stock on its way will arrive soon, so ordering for it again would buy the same pairs twice
It is optional, because on-order pairs never arrive
Pairs on order have already been sold
